blocks.text: Detention fee disputes usually stem from grey areas in your initial agreement. If your rate confirmation does not explicitly define the free time allowed at a facility, you have no baseline for the charge. When a carrier submits an invoice for two hours of detention, but the shipper log shows only forty-five minutes, the conflict begins. These discrepancies often arise from poor documentation or a lack of clear communication during the loading process.
The cost of unresolved freight disputes

Beyond the immediate financial impact, these disputes create massive administrative backlogs. Manual reconciliation is slow and prone to error. When you spend 15 minutes chasing a single document, you lose time that could be spent on higher-value tasks like sourcing new capacity. A lingering $15 million billing-exception backlog is a real risk for larger brokerages that do not have automated triage systems in place.
How to fix disputes without extra software

items: Standardize your rate confirmation templates to include specific detention terms.
Require carriers to submit time stamps or signed gate logs for all detention claims.
Use neutral, factual language in your emails to prevent emotional escalation.
Maintain a single source of truth in your TMS to verify charges against original contracts.
Establish a clear internal escalation procedure for when a dispute remains unresolved after three days.

faq.question: What is the best way to handle a carrier who insists on a fee I did not approve?
faq.answer: Ask for the supporting documentation, such as a signed gate log or timestamped photos. Refer back to the specific terms in your original, signed rate confirmation.

faq.question: How can I reduce the time spent on freight invoice disputes?
faq.answer: Automate your invoice triage by comparing incoming bills against your TMS rate confirmations. This flags mismatches early so you only deal with the exceptions.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with my TMS if it is a web-based app?
faq.answer: Yes. Since most modern TMS platforms run in Chrome or Safari on macOS, Lazur can see your screen, point at elements, and help you draft responses in your browser.
